extra.reason: Added tree-sitter defun navigation: treesit-defun-type-regexp (cons form with pkl-ts-mode--defun-p predicate) covers clazz, typeAlias, classMethod, objectMethod, and object-valued properties; scalar properties are excluded. treesit-defun-name-function reuses the imenu name helper, enabling which-function/add-log (e.g. Server.url). 7 navigation tests (class, method, object, typealias, scalar-skip, end-of-defun, qualified name) plus README docs. 52/52 tests pass, compile clean.

Won't do — superseded by the external 'expreg' package (by the treesit.el author). expreg's tree-sitter expander works generically with any mode that has a parser, so it already provides expand/contract structural selection in pkl-ts-mode (which creates a 'pkl parser) with no code in this package. Users bind expreg-expand to C-=.

Added Evil text object iO/aO for qualified names (member-access chain incl. trailing call, or qualifiedIdentifier), the W-to-w style larger sibling of the symbol object o. Tests pass under stub and real Evil; README documents it.

Fixed by declaring only the args each text object body uses: (count) for range-only objects, (count &optional beg end) for paragraph objects — evil-define-text-object's canonical arglist. Investigated alternatives against both NonGNU 1.15.0 and MELPA 20260603: underscore-prefix fails stable ('not left unused'), full named args fail rolling ('unused'), and &rest unused (evil-textobj-tree-sitter's workaround) also fails rolling under -Werror. Only declaring exactly what's used is clean on both. compile-evil + full test-evil green on both channels + stub; a durable code comment guards against regression.

Added rolling-Evil dimension to CI: matrix include with stable (29.4, 30.1, blocking) and rolling (30.1, non-blocking via continue-on-error). Install step enables MELPA for the rolling channel (its date-versioned master snapshot outranks the NonGNU release). YAML validated.
